Build reports from measurement, G/D-study or residual results

Source: R/api-results.R
mfrm_report.Rd

mfrm_report() connects existing measurement results, G/D-study results and residual exploration to tables, Markdown and HTML. It does not refit, recompute diagnostics or create new inferential support. Pass G/D-study and mfrm_residual_network() objects directly. Rater/halo networks and fit_rater_network() results also connect directly, retaining definitions, unavailable pairs, network fit, cluster-bootstrap contrasts and ERGM checks. Attach previously calculated G/D intervals explicitly. See the dedicated section below and the editable templates/gtheory-report.Rmd.

For an mfrm_results() object, it turns the comprehensive first-screen result into a first-screen table, section plan, claim-readiness table, report-gap table, report-index table, template-index table, fit-criteria table, result-specific fit evidence summaries, fit-reporting wording templates, precision/separation reporting templates, bias/DFF reporting templates, misfit/pathway reporting templates, linking/anchor reporting templates, ZSTD-convention table, evidence-boundary table, next-action table, and optional Markdown or HTML report. For mfrm_results() inputs, except for the individual rater sheet, the object and its table list retain the exact source-fit fit_readiness* tables from mfrm_results(); report synthesis does not reinterpret or upgrade them. The decision table translates that same record into interpretation, formal-inference, reason, and next-action text.

Usage

mfrm_report(
  x,
  style = c("qc", "apa", "validation", "reviewer", "technical", "rater"),
  output = c("object", "markdown", "html", "tables"),
  facet = NULL,
  rater = NULL,
  audience = c("rater", "researcher"),
  label = NULL,
  max_cases = 5,
  interval = NULL,
  intervals = NULL,
  study_context = NULL
)

Arguments

x

An mfrm_results() object, a supported G/D-study or network result, or output from estimate_bias(), estimate_all_bias(), review_mfrm_anchors(), build_linking_review() or build_model_choice_review().

style

Report emphasis. "qc" is the default first-screen report. "apa" emphasizes manuscript wording, "validation" emphasizes the validity-argument boundary, "reviewer" emphasizes reviewer response preparation, and "technical" emphasizes appendix/reproducibility routes. "rater" creates a standalone individual feedback sheet from saved native additive RSM/PCM or two-family GPCM MML results; it requires facet and rater.

output

Return format: "object" for an mfrm_report object (mfrm_rater_feedback when style = "rater"), "markdown" for a character scalar, "html" for a temporary HTML file, or "tables" for the report's named data-frame list.

facet

For style = "rater", the fitted non-Person facet representing raters, for example "Rater". It is not inferred from the column name.

rater

For style = "rater", one character level of facet.

audience

For a rater sheet, "rater" gives plain-language guidance; "researcher" adds the model, estimator and diagnostic basis. Both use the same saved numerical values and omit source identifiers.

label

Optional recipient-facing label for a rater sheet. The default is "Selected rater"; even the selected source identifier is not copied. Any identifying information explicitly supplied here will be displayed.

max_cases

Maximum number of saved unexpected ratings in a rater sheet, ordered by absolute standardized residual. Default 5; use 0 to omit individual cases. This is not a misfit threshold.

interval

Optional name of a saved fixed-facet interval attachment in x$facet_intervals for an additive-model rater sheet, or a saved component slope interval in x$gpcm_inference for two-family GPCM. The attachment must contain the selected individual coefficient, not just a difference involving it. A single matching attachment is used automatically. Multiple matching attachments require an explicit choice. No interval is calculated here.

intervals

For a G/D-study only, saved confint(x) output or a list of such results. Source, design and target context are checked. NULL reports point estimates without intervals; logical values do not trigger computation. Old component intervals lacking source context must be recreated with the current confint(g). This differs from singular interval, which selects an attachment for an individual rater sheet.

study_context

Optional named character vector of study declarations, for example c(question = "...", rating_unit = "...", score_direction = "Higher means easier to understand", rubric = "1 = very difficult; 9 = very easy", transformation = "None", anchor_source = "..."). Names must be unique; values must be nonmissing and nonblank. The same declaration can accompany separate measurement, G/D and feedback reports when their meanings match. It is retained in $study_context, $tables$study_context, Markdown, HTML and report appendix export. These are user declarations, not model-verified facts: they never recode data, reverse parameter signs, validate anchors or change eligibility. For a recipient-facing rater sheet, supply only context intended for that recipient; text is copied verbatim.

Value

Depending on output, an mfrm_report object, a Markdown character scalar, an mfrm_report_html object, or a named list of data frames. For style = "rater", object output has class mfrm_rater_feedback and contains title, label, audience, review, guidance, notes, tables and markdown. It does not contain the original result object.

Details

The intended workflow is:

  1. Create res <- mfrm_results(fit, include = ...).

  2. Inspect summary(res)$triage and summary(res)$next_actions.

  3. Create report <- mfrm_report(res, style = "qc").

  4. Read summary(report) and report$first_screen before opening detailed report tables.

  5. Use report$report_index to choose the next PrimaryTable, TemplateTable, plot route, or export route.

  6. Use report$template_index before copying APA/QC/validation wording.

  7. Use style = "apa", "validation", "reviewer", or "technical" only when that reporting question is needed.

Report rows deliberately distinguish evidence from claims. The testlet and random-rater route is a smaller stored-result report: all supported styles (excluding "rater") retain numerical checks, data usage, interval meanings and supplied predictions/intervals. When saved scores include a scoring roster, the scoring_roster table preserves its rows, identifiers and omitted scores; testlet scoring_blocks separately summarizes observed blocks. Older results without a roster do not reconstruct one from calibration rows. It does not supply ordinary residual diagnostics or fit/APA wording templates; template_index is empty. See the model-specific section in mfrm_results() for supported tables and plots. The Response residuals row distinguishes an unsupplied saved mfrm_response_diagnostics() result (not_computed) from a supplied result with no available observed-row results (unavailable) or results requiring review. If needed, compute these diagnostics separately for a numerically ready fit and attach them through mfrm_results(fit, response_diagnostics = diagnostics). Available summaries remain descriptive (caveat): ordinary-model cutoffs do not apply, and they do not establish model adequacy. Report creation never computes the missing diagnostics. Older result bundles can be passed to mfrm_report() again to update the report; previously exported files retain their original text.

For ordinary models, the first_screen table is the compact entry point: it gives an overall row and one row per major evidence area with status, readiness, main issue, next action, and primary route. The summary.mfrm_report method summarizes that first screen into immediate actions, optional not-requested sections, claim-readiness counts, report gaps, and template-boundary rows without introducing a new pass/fail decision. The default print method follows the same short reading order and does not print every detailed evidence table. HTML output places the same reader guidance and report-summary tables before the full Markdown text so the browser view starts from the first-screen route. The report_index table is the detailed evidence-route index: it lists the major report areas, evidence status, readiness label, review-signal count, and the primary/template tables, evidence routes, template routes, plot routes, export route, and mfrm_results(include = ...) preset to inspect next. In ordinary use, open detailed tables through the PrimaryTable and TemplateTable columns rather than scanning every element of report$tables. The template_index table then stacks all fit, precision, bias, misfit, and linking wording templates into a single boundary/claim-strength index before users drill into the area-specific template tables. The claim_readiness table marks which report claims are ready, caveated, unavailable, or require additional requested sections. The report_gaps table turns those statuses into follow-up actions. The fit-specific tables keep multiple MnSq threshold profiles, observed fit-status counts, and engine-vs-FACETS-style ZSTD conventions visible, including the small-df/capping boundary used for FACETS-style ZSTD review. They summarize the stored fit_measures component from mfrm_results(); mfrm_report() itself does not recompute diagnostics. The fit_reporting_templates table turns those counts into cautious reporting language while keeping MnSq, ZSTD standardization, df sensitivity, and separation/reliability in separate sentences. All reporting-template tables share EvidenceTable, EvidenceRoute, BoundaryType, ClaimStrength, and RecommendedUse columns so each template can be traced back to its evidence and claim boundary. The default RecommendedUse is "report_with_context"; more restrictive rows request evidence, identify a methods or appendix caveat, or require targeted follow-up. template_index stacks those columns across all template areas so report authors can review unsupported or caveated wording before opening the full template text. The precision_reporting_templates table does the same for separation, reliability, and strata using the stored precision review and diagnostics$reliability. precision_by_facet preserves every stored facet row, original values, missing-value reasons and inference flags. Templates report model and fit-adjusted indices separately for each facet; they are not confidence bounds. Cross-facet ranges in the compatibility summary are not an overall reliability coefficient. A Person separation index computed with EAP/posterior SD is not posterior-variance EAP reliability; this report does not compute that different index. fit_calculation_basis identifies the recorded target of the MnSq tables, including EAP plug-in and imported source definitions. Missing metadata stays unrecorded. Rebuild reports from saved results to obtain these explanations; no re-estimation is needed. The bias_reporting_templates table is available when the source result was built with include = "bias" and keeps facet-level screens, interaction-bias contrasts, DFF follow-up, and fairness conclusions in separate sections. The misfit_reporting_templates table is available when the source result was built with include = "misfit_review" and keeps unexpected responses, displacement, pathway-map evidence, and case-review actions separate. The linking_reporting_templates table is available when the source result was built with include = "linking" and keeps anchor readiness, drift review, equating-chain review, and GPCM support boundaries separate. For example, fit and separation are not collapsed into a single pass/fail statement; bias screens are not treated as final fairness conclusions; pathway/misfit rows are case-review prompts; and drift/equating claims require multiple fitted forms or waves.

Anchor, bias and model-choice modules

Use mfrm_report(review_mfrm_anchors(...)) before anchored fitting, mfrm_report(build_linking_review(...)) for saved link evidence, mfrm_report(estimate_bias(...)) for a prespecified interaction, and mfrm_report(estimate_all_bias(...)) for a collection of exploratory screens. Collection reports keep every requested interaction in tables$overview, all retained cells in tables$bias_cells with an Interaction key, failed pairs in tables$errors, and calculation settings/history and facet directions. Failed pairs remain visible even with keep_errors = FALSE; unavailable screens are not reported as negative results. No collection-wide multiplicity adjustment is added. Use mfrm_report(build_model_choice_review(...)) for candidate-model roles and comparability. Reporting does not fit a new model, select new interaction cells, calculate a missing LRT or test anchor invariance. Full bias cells and anchor values remain alongside compact summaries; source objects and unavailable states are preserved. style = "rater" continues to require individual feedback from mfrm_results(). Supply study_context to keep rubric direction, transformations, anchor provenance and the question with the report. A shared declaration does not establish equivalence between a raw G-study score and a latent MFRM measure. See the editable templates/assessment-review.Rmd for separate modules using bundled data and a saved report archive.

Planning and numerical review

Pass recommend_mfrm_design() results directly to preserve the planning target, threshold sources, all candidate designs and long criterion outcomes. Facet calibration reliability is not inter-rater agreement. Recommendations apply to the simulated conditions; no universal sample size is inferred. Main-effects mfrm_d_study() results also enter directly. These reports preserve residual-scaling assumptions and unavailable coefficients separately from full interaction-component G-studies. Newly created projections retain source components and observed counts; missing historical metadata are labelled not_recorded without refitting. Intervals are unsupported for this approximation and for simulation recommendations. Native measurement reports include numerical_review: separate evidence and next actions for optimization, curvature, starts, integration and replay. This table neither reruns diagnostics nor changes inferential readiness.

G/D-study and residual-exploration reports

Saved Stan/brms summaries read by read_mfrm_posterior() also enter this route directly. Reports retain their credible-interval level, fixed values, priors, model-data identity and sampling review. They do not calculate new intervals, native MML diagnostics, prior sensitivity or posterior predictions.

Pass mfrm_g_study(), mfrm_d_study(), mfrm_multivariate_d_compare() or mfrm_residual_network() output directly, without mfrm_results(). The non-rater styles all preserve the same complete domain-specific tables and interpretation notes. Report creation never refits, clusters or computes intervals. The overall review status asks for substantive study context; it is not a numerical convergence or formal-inference assessment.

G/D tables retain observed counts separately from future plans, fixed score/composite weights, signed covariance components, component policy, G/Phi, universe/error variances, measurement SEM and unavailable states. Saved component or plan/contrast intervals retain their methods, assumptions and any separate interval center. Without supplied intervals the report explicitly states not_requested. Paired-delta comparisons have their own report, preserving their shared-source covariance and approximation. These are observed-score studies, not latent-trait fits or MFRM separation reliability. Brennan (2003) explains why coefficients should be accompanied by error variances; Jiang et al. (2022) emphasize uncertainty and studied design conditions. Their findings do not validate every interval method supplied here.

Use build_summary_table_bundle(report) for all numerical and contextual tables, apa_table(report, which = "coefficients") for a selected D-study table, and export_summary_appendix() for CSV/HTML. summary(report) keeps the full evidence tables in evidence_tables; top_n does not truncate them. Save the complete report/source with saveRDS() for replay. Source archives can contain participant identifiers and require sharing review. The installed editable template is located by system.file("templates", "gtheory-report.Rmd", package = "mfrmr").

Residual reports retain all nodes and pairs, overlap, threshold settings and cluster availability. They support exploratory review; they do not establish dimensions, rater quality, stable classes or causal relationships. See mfrm_residual_network() for unsupervised learning, validation and the distinct role of supervised random forests.

Stored agreement in ordinary-model reports

When diagnostics are present, the narrative and tables$interrater_interpretation distinguish observed agreement from the fitted-model expected baseline and from separation reliability. tables$interrater_summary retains the stored numerical summary unchanged. The denominator counts matched-context opportunities across rater pairs, not independent people. Unavailable values, zero matched opportunities and an absent stored summary are described explicitly; no missing agreement statistic is computed during reporting. Reports without diagnostics retain their existing component-status explanation rather than inventing values. These summaries share their interpretation with build_apa_outputs(). See interrater_agreement_table() for calculations and matching conventions. Markdown and HTML contain the same explanation; export with export_mfrm_results(res, include = "report") to retain the summary and interpretation as CSV files as well. Existing saved APA drafts retain their original wording until regenerated with build_apa_outputs() and the same saved fit/diagnostics. Regeneration does not refit the model.

Two-family GPCM reports

Reports retain all saved non-Person fitted locations, category steps and component slopes. Locations identify their centering constraint; steps identify their owner and level and are centered offsets, not standalone thresholds. Separately computed experimental location/contrast intervals from mfrm_facet_intervals() may be attached; step intervals remain unavailable. The Markdown view shows up to 20 rows per table with a notice; complete tables remain in $tables and CSV exports. Report styles do not change inferential support.

Corrected JML reports

Results from an explicit jml_correction_order have an estimator-specific report of saved estimates, numerical status and RootSE interpretation. The report does not contain ordinary fit tests or structural confidence intervals. The "rater" style is unavailable for this estimator. Saved mfrm_response_diagnostics() output adds conditional response means, probabilities and descriptive residual summaries, with unavailable indices and their reasons retained. These do not classify rater quality. See mfrm_results() and the Corrected JML section of fit_mfrm().

Individual rater sheets

Use mfrm_report(res, style = "rater", facet = "Rater", rater = "R01", output = "html") to create a temporary HTML sheet. Open its $path, review it, and copy that file to a permanent location for distribution. HTML is self-contained, includes print styling and category-use bars with numerical tables, and does not load external resources. Page count depends on content and browser print settings; this is not a PDF export API. After reviewing the sheet, use file.copy(sheet$path, recipient_file) to keep it at a chosen HTML path. To prepare sheets in a later session, save the complete res with base::saveRDS() and reload it with base::readRDS(). The RDS file retains fitted data and identifiers for the analyst; it is not the recipient's sheet. Reloading and reporting reuse the saved analysis without updating it for new ratings. output = "tables" includes an interpretation_notes table with the overall review, audience-specific guidance and section explanations. Keep this table with the numerical tables when saving CSV files or sharing them. These explanations are the sheet's fixed, recipient-safe text; free-form notes from the source analysis are not copied. The same table is available in the sheet object's $tables. HTML and Markdown show the explanations beside their sections, without duplicating them as another table. The uncertainty table retains Available and a recipient-safe Reason, distinguishing constraint-fixed values, insufficient independent-cluster information, unusable variance/bounds and failed numerical/profile checks where the saved diagnostics identify the cause. If the interval is unavailable, both bounds are missing in the sheet, even when the analyst's saved result retains one computed endpoint. This does not mean zero uncertainty or an unbounded interval. The original saved analysis is unchanged; unidentified reasons direct the recipient to the analyst. Printing the sheet also shows interval availability and its explanation. Recreate sheets from saved mfrm_results objects to obtain these fields; reading an older sheet does not update its contents.

The additive RSM/PCM sheet includes scoring tendency (severity), exposure, available saved fixed-facet uncertainty, ordinary Infit/Outfit, category use and selected unexpected ratings. Severity is oriented so that positive values mean lower expected scores. Its zero is the fitted model reference, not necessarily the average of the other raters; custom centering and anchors matter. Model scores and expected scores stay on the fitted category coding. The category table also shows the original numeric scores when a mapping exists. Exposure and category percentages count retained rows without weights; weight sums are reported separately. Neither is planned-design completion.

Supply matching diagnose_mfrm() output to mfrm_results() to include fit and unexpected ratings. Attach mfrm_facet_intervals() output through intervals = list(raters = ci) for supported MML fixed-facet intervals. JML sheets can show saved descriptive diagnostics but do not gain formal fixed-facet intervals. Inspect the complete saved interval result and its numerical cautions before sharing; free-form cautions are not copied into the recipient's sheet. Missing sections explain the missing input. Ineligible source fits retain a prominent review notice. Severity is not rater quality, and no automatic misfit cutoff, exclusion decision or diagnostic accuracy claim is added. These sheets do not support one-family GPCM, fitted interactions, imported fits, testlet or shared-random-rater models; use their specific results and reports because their effects and diagnostics differ.

For two-family GPCM MML, the same entry creates an experimental descriptive sheet. Select the modeled rater facet explicitly; either slope owner is supported. It separates the fitted location from the component slope, retains their distinct centering references, and reports category use, retained exposure and how many levels of the other facet were observed. Category-step offsets are shown only when this facet owns the steps. They are centered offsets, not standalone thresholds. This individual sheet does not display location or step intervals; use the analyst report for separately requested location intervals. A larger slope is not evidence of competence or accuracy.

Attach saved confint.mfrm_fit() output from parm = "slopes" through intervals in mfrm_results() to include a matching experimental component-slope interval. interval chooses among named attachments; pointwise/Bonferroni meaning, profile/log-Wald method and unavailable bounds are retained. No location interval or test of rater differences is implied. Attach saved mfrm_response_diagnostics() output through response_diagnostics for same-data posterior residual summaries and cases. The sheet counts saved, available, unresolved and not-included rows separately; a summary average is unavailable if any saved row for that recipient is unresolved. These residuals have no expectation-one reference or calibrated cutoff, exclude calibration uncertainty and do not predict independent future ratings. Creating or reopening a sheet does not fit, integrate, compute intervals or diagnose new responses. Inspect the complete analyst results before sharing a sheet; numerical convergence does not qualify feedback decisions.

All four output formats use only selected numeric summaries and fixed explanatory text. They omit the source fit, Person identifiers, other rater identifiers, original row numbers, task labels and free-form source notes. Case numbers refer only to the displayed ordering. This prevents copying those identifier fields; it is not a guarantee against recognition from rating patterns, small groups or an explicitly supplied label. Review the content before sharing, and use max_cases = 0 when cases are unnecessary. Distribute the standalone sheet, not the comprehensive results/export bundle, which retains the original analysis. Rater-specific arguments are rejected with other report styles, even when explicitly supplied as NULL.

References

Brennan, R. L. (2003). Coefficients and indices in generalizability theory. CASMA Research Report No. 1, University of Iowa. https://education.uiowa.edu/sites/education.uiowa.edu/files/2026-04/casma-research-report-1-archived.pdf.

Jiang, Z., Raymond, M., DiStefano, C., Shi, D., Liu, R., & Sun, J. (2022). A Monte Carlo study of confidence interval methods for generalizability coefficient. Educational and Psychological Measurement, 82, 705–718. doi:10.1177/00131644211033899 .

See also

mfrm_results(), export_mfrm_results(), build_apa_outputs(), reporting_checklist(), mfrmr_output_guide()

Examples

# Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed.
# example("mfrm_report", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Load the package and example ratings
library(mfrmr)
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_operational")

# Fit these ratings; replace the data-loading line for your own analysis
fit <- fit_mfrm(
  data = ratings,
  person = "Person",
  facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  score = "Score",
  rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4, category_policy = "preserve",
  method = "MML",
  model = "RSM"
)

# Build results, then turn them into a report
res <- mfrm_results(fit)
report <- mfrm_report(res)

# Read the report and the issues to address
summary(report, view = "reader")
report$first_screen[, c("Area", "Status", "MainIssue", "NextAction")]
report$fit_calculation_basis
report$precision_by_facet[, c("Facet", "Levels", "Reliability",
                              "RealReliability", "InputUncertaintyBasis")]
contextual_report <- mfrm_report(res, study_context = c(
  rating_unit = "One Person by Rater by Criterion rating",
  score_direction = "Higher coded scores indicate more favorable performance",
  rubric = "Synthetic example: permitted scores 1 to 4", transformation = "None"
))
contextual_report$tables$study_context

# Select a recipient explicitly. Missing intervals are explained in the sheet.
recipient <- as.character(fit$prep$levels$Rater[1])
sheet <- mfrm_report(res, style = "rater", facet = "Rater",
                     rater = recipient, output = "html", max_cases = 0)
sheet$path
# Review in a browser, then choose a permanent path for continuing work.
recipient_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".html")
stopifnot(file.copy(sheet$path, recipient_file, overwrite = FALSE))
} # }
